text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P0 triggered — elevated error rate on hosted inference for model variant redwood-ggml-v2 in us-west-2. Automatic warmup jobs failing. Linking incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2035009876
oncall-ml-tanya: ack. pinging runtime + infra. starting triage now. initial hypothesis: OOM at model load or deserialization errors during warmup.
mike-ops: seeing a bunch of pods in CrashLoopBackOff in us-west-2-gpu-pool-3. kube events show OOMKill on gunicorn-warmup containers. snippet: ```
Apr 12 17:03:21 kubelet[1234]: Container crashed with OOMKilled
runtime: goroutine 45 [running]:
#0 0x7f... cuMemAlloc failed with error OUT_OF_MEMORY
```
alex-runtime: same logs on our side — warmup worker logs include `deserialize: unexpected EOF` and then a compile timeout: `tx_compile: timeout after 120s`. I think a large shard/partial checkpoint is corrupt or an incompatible serialization format hit the new loading path.
sara-sre: metrics: 503 rate spiked from 0.4% -> 12% for the redwood-ggml-v2 route between 17:02-17:12. Affected requests ~900rps -> ~100rps failures depending on routing. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dash/models/redwood-ggml-v2/errors
emily-support: high-usage customers on that model include SpinLoop and Nookly — SpinLoop has an open support ticket (INC-9876) and is reporting timeouts from their end. I'm drafting a status update.
infra-bot: Autoscaler attempted to scale GPU pool but hit quota. Current GPU free capacity in us-west-2: 0. Suggest fallback to CPU-quantized variant or route to another region.
oncall-ml-tanya: proposal (short): 1) Disable warmup jobs for redwood-ggml-v2 (stop causing OOMs) 2) Update routing policy to reroute requests to redwood-ggml-v2-int8-fallback (quantized CPU/GPU mixed) 3) Restart 2 affected nodes after cordon/drain 4) If errors persist, roll back today's model-serving runtime change pushed at 16:50. I'll split tasks.
mike-ops: starting node drain on gw-node-12 and gw-node-15 now. ETA for node reprovisioning ~10m. `kubectl drain gw-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
alex-runtime: I'll push a hot config to route 30% -> fallback immediately, then increase if errors drop. curl command to update route: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/route/update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route":"/gen/v2","model":"redwood-ggml-v2","fallback":"redwood-ggml-v2-int8-fallback","percentage":30}'
```
sara-sre: monitoring SLO windows. setting alert to mute non-critical noise for the warmup-runbook channel. Keeping P0 page open.
emily-support: Sent interim message to SpinLoop: "We're aware of elevated 5xx for requests to redwood-ggml-v2. Engineers are rerouting traffic to fallback models and performing node restarts. We'll update in 15m."
infra-bot: fallback route applied by runtime-config service. Confirmed: 30% traffic -> redwood-ggml-v2-int8-fallback. Autoscaler still limited but fallback uses different pool.
oncall-ml-tanya: quick check — after initial 30% shift, error rate dropped from 12% -> 4.5% in 2 minutes. We'll ramp to 70% if stable.
mike-ops: nodes drained and restarted. Kube events show pods recreated on different nodes and warmup disabled for the problematic job.
alex-runtime: bumping fallback to 70% now. update command posted.
sara-sre: after 70% shift, 5xx rate down to 0.9% and latency within SLO. Marking customer-impact as degraded -> partial.
emily-support: updating tickets and customer status page. Notifying SpinLoop with ETA for full remediation.
oncall-ml-tanya: quick postmortem plan: capture warmup logs for failing tasks, fetch the serialized blob that caused `unexpected EOF` if possible, run checksum across shards, and run a canary load locally. Also revert today's small runtime tweak if we find correlation. Assigning owners: alex-runtime for config & logs, mike-ops for node reprovision, sara-sre for monitoring, emily-support for customer comms.
incident-bot: Note: if this extends beyond 18:30 UTC, handoff to oncall-ml-jordan will be triggered automatically.
oncall-ml-tanya: current status summary for handoff: - Root cause suspected: corrupted/partial checkpoint or new deserialization path triggering OOMs during warmup + compile timeouts. - Mitigations in-place: warmup disabled, traffic routed to int8 fallback (70%), restarted affected nodes. - Customer impact: partial (some requests still routed to primary until full cutover; SpinLoop experiencing timeouts earlier, now improved). - Open actions: fetch failing checkpoint blob, run local canary with full-load, investigate runtime changes at 16:50.
oncall-ml-jordan: thanks for the handoff — I'm oncall now and monitoring. If anything re-escalates ping me directly.
alex-runtime: logs pulled and uploaded to shared bucket s3://redwood-incident-logs/2035009876/ — I included the `deserialize` stack traces and the failing shard meta. Preliminary checksum shows mismatched shard sizes for shard_23.
mike-ops: reprovision completed, nodes healthy. We removed the old warmup job definition from the daemonset that was spawning with aggressive mem limits.
sara-sre: final check: error rate steady ~0.6% for last 10m, latency normalized. I'll keep a 30-minute watch window.
emily-support: sent final update to affected customers: "We implemented a fallback routing and node restarts; errors reduced significantly. Engineering is investigating root cause and will provide a follow-up postmortem."
oncall-ml-tanya: thanks team. I'm closing the immediate pager. Will follow up with a postmortem doc and action items. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Pager closed by oncall-ml-tanya at 18:28 UTC. Resolution: traffic routed to fallback + node restarts; further investigation ongoing.
